questions.question: Describe the three somatotypes and give a sporting example for each.
questions.correctAnswer: Endomorph: high body fat, round and soft body shape, wide waist and hips. Example: sumo wrestler or rugby prop forward. Mesomorph: muscular, athletic build, broad shoulders and narrow waist, low body fat. Example: sprinter or gymnast. Ectomorph: lean and thin, low body fat and muscle mass, narrow shoulders and long limbs. Example: marathon runner or high jumper.

questions.question: Explain why an endomorph is well-suited to being a rugby prop forward.
questions.correctAnswer: An endomorph is well-suited to being a rugby prop forward because their large body mass provides stability in the scrum - they are harder to push backwards. Their wide build and heavy frame anchor the scrum, allowing them to generate a powerful pushing force against the opposition pack. questions.question: Why is an ectomorph the ideal somatotype for a marathon runner?
questions.correctAnswer: An ectomorph is ideal for marathon running because their low body weight reduces the energy cost of every stride - carrying less mass over 26.2 miles requires significantly less energy than a heavier build. questions.question: Explain why most athletes are not purely one somatotype. Use a specific sporting example.
questions.correctAnswer: Most athletes are not purely one somatotype because different sports require a combination of physical characteristics that no single somatotype provides alone.
